# Problem

After all skill fixes land on dev, the full test suite must be verified green before the epic can be advanced to in_review.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Run the full test suite via `python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` (or `pytest -q`) and confirm 0 failures.
2. If any pre-existing red on dev is encountered, triage into a critical test-failure work item (SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5 precedent) and stop.
3. `wl sync` changes.
4. Report full suite result on the epic work item.
5. If suite green, advance epic stage to in_review.

## Related

- **SA-0MUUI6ZCX001RO8V** — Epic (parent).
data.title: Verify full test suite green and sync on epic completion

## Problem Statement

The agent-log-review skill must be invocable by agents via `/skill:agent-log-review`, follow the project's skill conventions (`SKILL.md` + `scripts/` + `tests/`), and be documented in `docs/dev/` so maintainers can understand and extend it.

## Goal

As an agent operator, I want to invoke `/skill:agent-log-review` and get a structured report plus auto-created improvement work items; as a maintainer, I want reference documentation covering the design, CLI usage, and extension points.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md` exists with frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and an invocation section documenting `/skill:agent-log-review`, its flags (`--max-sessions`, `--json`, `--dry-run`, `--parent-id`, `--model`), and its outputs.
- [ ] `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md` documents: architecture (parser → heuristics → LLM → report → worklog integration), v3 session-log format consumed, privacy/redaction rules, and test strategy.
- [ ] `SKILL.md` follows the conventions of existing skills (e.g. `skill/audit/SKILL.md`): description, inputs, results/outputs, process, bundled resources.
- [ ] README or docs index updated if the project lists skills there.
- [ ] Code comments in `agent_log_review.py` document the public functions and the v3 format assumptions.
- [ ] The skill is discoverable: running the skill directory's tests passes, and invoking the script with `--help` prints usage.
- [ ] A smoke test (or documented manual check) verifies the skill runs end-to-end against a fixture session directory.

## Constraints

- Documentation-only for the SKILL.md and reference doc; no behaviour changes to the script in this item.
- Follow UK English spelling and existing doc conventions.
- No changes to `skill/`, `command/` infra outside the new skill directory and `docs/dev/` (unless README indexing requires an entry).

## Key Files

- `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md` — new skill definition and invocation docs
- `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md` — maintainer reference
- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — ensure docstrings/comments are complete

## Dependencies

- Features 1–5 — documentation describes the implemented behaviour, so it lands last.
data.title: Agent log review: SKILL.md definition and reference docs

# Migrate implement.py repo/worktree fixtures to git_sandbox

Parent: SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0

## Goal

Route every real-git invocation in the `implement.py` test fixtures through
`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` so a leaked repository-overriding environment
cannot redirect the fixture away from its `tmp_path` sandbox.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixtures in `tests/test_implement_worktree_repo_root.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_submodules.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py` and
  `tests/test_implement_code_freeze_gate.py` use `gs.init_repo`,
  `gs.commit_all`, `gs.add_worktree` and `gs.run_git`; no bare
  `subprocess.run(["git", …])` remains in these files.
- [ ] Each migrated fixture helper has a behavioural regression test proving a
  leaked `GIT_DIR` cannot redirect it (victim repo unchanged; the fixture repo
  resolves under `tmp_path`), mirroring
  `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py::TestEnvironmentIsolation` and
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py::TestRepoHelpersAreHermetic`.
- [ ] Every `implement.py` subprocess runner in these files passes
  `gs.sanitized_git_env()` so a leaked override cannot reach the child's git
  invocations (as already done in
  `tests/test_implement_worktree_enforcement.py::_run_violation_check`).
- [ ] `default_branch` is set correctly so fixtures that relied on a `dev`
  branch (e.g. `git branch dev` after init) do not create a spurious or
  duplicate branch.
- [ ] Fixture identity is injected via the sandbox (`-c user.name=… -c user.email=…`) rather than relying on a repo-local `git config` in the helper; any remaining identity `config` in a migrated helper is explicit and deliberate.
- [ ] All existing behavioural assertions in the five files pass unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace each fixture's `git init` + `config user.*` + `add` + `commit` +
  `branch dev` sequence with `gs.init_repo(..., default_branch="dev")` +
  `gs.commit_all(...)`; replace `git worktree add` with `gs.add_worktree(...)`.
- Keep subprocess-runner helper scripts, but spawn them with
  `env=gs.sanitized_git_env()`.
- Add one hermetic regression test per migrated fixture (victim + leaked
  `GIT_DIR`).

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_worktree_repo_root.py`
- `tests/test_implement_submodules.py`
- `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py`
- `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py`
- `tests/test_implement_code_freeze_gate.py`

## Dependencies

F1 (tracer-bullet recipe and regression template).
data.title: Migrate implement.py repo/worktree fixtures to git_sandbox

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/test_wl_sync_no_commits.py::_init_no_commit_repo` uses

  `commit_all`); the initial-commit step in

  `gs.commit_all`.
- [ ] Each migrated fixture helper has a behavioural regression test proving a

# Full-suite verification, docs and final bare-git sweep

Parent: SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0

## Goal

Close out the migration: prove the repo is free of the non-hermetic pattern
(within the documented exclusions), that the full suite is green, and that the
documentation reflects the final state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The full project suite passes via `/skill:test` (`run_tests.py --scope
  full`) with the migrated helpers in place; any failures are triaged through
  the triage skill.
- [ ] A repo-wide AST sweep confirms no test helper under `tests/` or
  `skill/**/tests/` invokes `git` via a bare `subprocess.run(["git", …])`, with
  the documented exclusions (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` embedded
  string-literal mutation proofs, which must not be routed through the
  sandbox).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any `docs/dev/` entries such as `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` documents the final migrated state
  (including `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py`'s env-only treatment), and
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern #7 is updated only if
  the migration revealed a gap.
- [ ] No test depends on ambient git identity or a leaked environment (fixture
  identity is injected via the sandbox).
- [ ] Findings that are out of scope (e.g. new test-quality issues) are
  recorded as linked work items rather than folded into this item.

## Minimal Implementation

- Run `/skill:test` at full scope; triage failures.
- Re-run the AST sweep and record the result as a work-item comment.
- Update the docs to match the final state.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`

## Dependencies

F1, F2, F3, F4, F5 (all migrations must land first).
data.title: Full-suite verification, docs, final bare-git sweep

Discovered-from:SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS.

## Goal

Prevent recurrence of the author-identity-gate refusal by adding `pi@local` to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` (project scope), so future pi-session-authored worklog sync commits pass the gate.

## Background

Operator decision (2026-10-16, SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS Decisions+Appendix): add `pi@local` to the allow list for this project. Intentional consequence: the project gate accepts `pi@local` authors; the empty-email gate is never bypassed; arbitrary foreign emails remain refused. The general guard `scripts/check_git_identity.py` must NOT be hardened to flag `pi@local` (that would contradict this allow-list).

**Why this is the durable fix:** the 4 offending commits and 3 older `pi@local` commits (7 total) remain in the shared `refs/worklog/data` history. A fresh clone has no `last-synced-ref`, so the gate scans the entire remote ref history and would refuse again until this allow-list entry lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `pi@local` is added to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` (project scope), with a comment explaining the deliberate widening and referencing SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS.
- [ ] **AC2** The regression test child (`Author-gate allow-list regression tests`) is green and its red-before/green-after evidence is recorded.
- [ ] **AC3** `check_git_identity.py` is unchanged (no new hardening flagging `pi@local`); its existing test suite stays green.

## Key Files

- `.worklog/config.yaml`

## Dependencies

- Blocked-by: SA-0MVBD5MXS007WJT0 (Author-gate allow-list regression tests — TDD contract first).

## Deliverables

- Updated `.worklog/config.yaml` + passing tests + commit comment.
data.title: Add pi@local to syncAllowedAuthors
